Can you fuzz this in a way that's integrated into the build system? In the case of adding something to `examples/` I expect we can make it consume/produce on stdin/stdout, which also gives us a path for fuzzing it (e.g. via afl++). But failing that I'd like to have the libfuzzer glue.
I think I'd like to see something that makes use of this in perhaps an `examples/` directory, or at least some more info in `docs/` for these types of things.
will do.
I'll investigate.
Added an example.
I added a libfuzzer test.  I might need a hint on how to fuzz with the example.  Matt had said something in the fuzz readme about afl-fuzz needing a gui?
`platform_pd.h` for consistency with `firmware_fd.h`? I realise `fd` is a defined concept in DSP0267 while `pd` is not in DSP0248, but I think we might as well follow.
ok.  just to make sure we are on the same page - pd = platform device?
Yeah, "platform device" was what I had in mind.
Done
Does it also setup the allocated memory? I think it probably should.
It does.  will update the comment.
Done

Perhaps this should be incorporated in the setup phase. That way the instance is either initialised properly or not?

If we use an ops struct instead we can make it an extensible struct, which allows for future expansion of handled ops.

An ops struct is how I started.  I switched to this approach because I was concerned about our ability to ever stabilize the API.  Maybe that isn't a real concern?

> If we use an ops struct instead we can make it an extensible struct, which allows for future expansion of handled ops.

Is there a pattern for doing this without breaking clients (assuming that is a concern) ?

> Is there a pattern for doing this without breaking clients (assuming that is a concern) ?

I think I answered my own question.  It would just be the same pattern as pldm_platform_pd.

There's some discussion of techniques here that I think is instructive:

https://lwn.net/Articles/830666/

We've used similar for the firmware update package parser structs.
Done
